bullets: Report to our Co-founder / Head of Product, Kapil Kale
Own new product areas before they have a team. Develop a thesis, do the research, size the opportunity, and make a recommendation: spin up a squad, build it lean, hand it off, or…
Turn research into shovel-ready work. Your output is briefs, prototypes, and specs that a squad can pick up and build immediately.
Move quickly using AI. Use agents to dig through customer tickets, sales calls, usage data, and competitor research. Ship clickable prototypes in days to test ideas with real…
Run projects that don't need a full squad. Some work is worth doing but too small for a team. You'll drive these end-to-end with engineers from existing squads.
Own your team's roadmap. Work with stakeholders to figure out what to build and when. When the path isn't obvious, your job is to create clarity.
Do the research. User interviews, market analysis, competitive teardowns, data digs. Whatever it takes to back up your thinking.
Move quickly using AI. Use AI agents to dig through customer tickets, sales calls, usage data, and competitor research. Use prototypes to illustrate approaches.
Partner with design and engineering through the build. Designers refine the UX, engineers estimate and build, you unblock and keep scope honest.
Work async. Most product work here happens in writing. If you're used to running product through meetings, this will feel different.
Own product priorities across Platform. Work with each team's engineering manager, our Director of Engineering for Platform, and stakeholders to identify problems, set priorities…
Work closely with engineers. Understand technical constraints and evaluate tradeoffs with engineers to choose solutions that balance security, usability, and effort.
Frame up problems. You’ll be expected to explain what problems we are solving and why. This helps our engineers and designers understand how to solve those problems.
Conduct research and analysis. In order to frame those problems well, you’ll need to collect supporting evidence–from user interviews, market research, and competitive analysis.
Work with designers and engineers to devise solutions. PMs set requirements and then work with designers and engineers to select appropriate solutions.
